2. The short fact is that the petitioner filed the aforesaid writ petition challenging the ex-parte decree passed in Money Suit No.19 of 2002 and the proceedings of Money Execution Case No.1 of 2006 corresponding to Money Execution Case No.85 of 2003 arising out of the said Money Suit No.19 of 2002 filed by the respondent No.1 against the petitioner in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong. The said writ petition was filed on the ground that the court at Chittagong which entertained and passed the ex-parte decree had no jurisdiction inasmuch   as the alleged cause of action arose in Dhaka and not in Chittagong and both the defendants were residents of places beyond the territorial jurisdiction   of the Chittagong District Court. Another ground for such challenge was that the said court passed the ex-parte decree without caring that the service return of summons of the suit was not received. 

 4. Mr. Shamsuddin Babul, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division erred in law in vacating the order of stay without considering the fact that the writ petition was filed on the ground that though the decree was passed against the petitioner and another but the execution court as per the prayer of the respondent issued an order of attachment of the property of the petitioner only leaving aside the other judgment debtor though both of the judgment debtors are equally liable for the same. He further submits that as per section 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the suit as filed was not within the jurisdiction of the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong and as such the ex-parte decree in the said Money Suit is without jurisdiction and void-ab initio and without any lawful authority and as such the High Court Division can look into the same in exercising jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. He lastly submits that going beyond the decree the judgment debtor filed the execution case and the execution court also going beyond the decree registered the execution case and also passed the order attaching the property of the petitioner which is clear violation of the provision of Code of Civil Procedure and without jurisdiction and in execution the writ jurisdiction the High Court Division can interfere with the said proceeding but without appreciating the same, the High Court Division came to a wrong decision and illegally vacated the order of stay and as such the same is liable to be interfered with.
